picks.note: Say the title out loud. "Huh? Bitch, you a shinto null. Mellow design ever kerosene…" is the body ("Habituation tonal melodies. I never care. Oh, seen a bear?…") re-spelled by sound. It's a homophonic translation. The local model's draft missed the joke and went looking for Shinto symbolism and a character named Eddie.

Prose built on vowel sounds: a paragraph that runs almost entirely on 'oy' (flamboyance, buoyancy, royalty recoiling noisily), then one soaked in 'ee' (reeling, seeking, steeped in the gleefulness streetlights). "Six quid for sick squids?" Read it aloud.

A 2014 post that riffs on information loss, entropy and gravity, then lands on 'our greatest achievement is not merely science, it is prescience.' It also has 'a ZIP file of you at the edge of the universe.' A decade later the miscdocs shelf is full of holographic-universe PDFs; this is the same itch, much earlier and funnier.
Three sentences, one of them the seed for the 'costs of legibility' trail: "Design and functionality grow unrelated as the gulf between perception and measurement grows." Then: "Who are you again?"

The author parodying their own grand theory: an 'Absurdity Patch 1.0' of the Weaver's Codex, 'mistranslated by a drunk probability squid.' Gravity is invented when spacetime slips on a banana peel. Kintsugi as a writing move: the crack gets gilded instead of hidden.

Reality documented as a software stack (Consciousness UI over Biological Service Mesh over Plasma Middleware over Quantum Foam API), written in full Gen-Z register: 'fr fr this the actual reality stack implementation no cap.'
"Welcome to the Titanic. Here is your paddle. Turn this ship around or you're fired." Workplace absurdism from 2015 that has aged into prophecy for anyone who has sat through a reorg.
Sound poetry from 2018: 'handwich the dock-spaggle, meep xir condequast wicktual despordeckedent wick stangible / BUNG STUNGIBLE.' Near-words that almost mean something, which is the whole trick.

Reads as edgy absurdism; is covert autobiography. 'I fell asleep many times. So often. Dozing, janitors checking to see if I'm okay… Lying under desks, sleeping on the clock' — the undiagnosed hypersomnia, in costume, a decade before it had a name. The evil in the title is the illness.

'Giants loom in the distance, leering, but you ignore them… I'm perfectly normal! you shout.' The giant is the author's own self-image — 'the chubby little giant Indian kid' from the spine essay. The shitposts were the pressure valve all along.

The keystone. Decades of dismissal resolved by AI-assisted self-diagnosis into an arachnoid web at T6-T7 — fewer than 200 documented cases. 'My chakra are blocked. Right below my heart.' Read this and the whole archive rearranges itself around it.

'An aphantasic technoshaman debugging reality one abstraction layer at a time.' The author can't picture anything internally — 'a realtime stream of log data' — and built a lab whose output is images and 3D scenes. This is the manifesto for everything on this dashboard.
